options.label: aoi · Aoi
options.who: 24, new hire in Facilities on room bookings, Japanese only, tennis beginner. The youngest of three, turned down by thirty companies, now in the new hires' dorm and hoping to run the island's event bookings one day.
questions: Her background explains why she joined in autumn: more than thirty companies turned her down, and she spent half a year at a karaoke front desk before Amakawa's autumn intake. Keep that, or should she be an ordinary graduate who is simply new? Default: keep it.

She was in a university tennis circle for four years and hardly played, so she knows how a club works but is still a beginner. Or should she never have held a racket before this Sunday? Default: the circle.

options.label: emi · Emi
options.who: 32, B2's team lead, native British English. Grew up in Reading, came to Amakawa as a translator, swims to keep her shoulders loose and wants a department head's job upstairs.
questions: Her name and her fluent Japanese come from a Japanese mother and an English father, and she grew up in Reading. The other way is two British parents, Emi short for Emily, and Japanese learned at university and at work. Which one? Default: the Japanese mother.

She wants a department head's job upstairs within five years, and the ten-year promise was partly for her own career. Does that ambition suit her, or should she want to stay on B2? Default: keep the ambition.
